moat_against: ROIC proxy negative every recent year (FY24 -13.4%, FY25 -5.6%, FY26 -2.5%) — GAAP operating income still negative because SBC consumes most of OCF
Hyperscalers and larger rivals on every flank: AWS OpenSearch (a fork of Elastic's own platform), Splunk/Cisco, Datadog, Microsoft and Google in search, observability and security
Open-source roots cut both ways: AWS offers a forked version, and native vector databases (Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate) plus MongoDB Atlas attack the AI-search growth story
No proven pricing power at the GAAP line: operating margin was still -1.9% in FY26 and -5% in Q1 FY27 despite ~75% gross margins
SBC was $303.3M TTM, about 86% of TTM operating cash flow, and the diluted share count grows 3.9%/yr
moat_for: Elasticsearch is the default search/data platform for a large developer base, embedded across search, observability and security on one stack
Data integration and cluster-tuning switching friction: workloads, indexes and pipelines are costly to migrate once in production
Gross margin 72-76% over the last five fiscal years (76.1% in FY26, 75.5% TTM) shows the product itself carries software economics
Enterprise cohort compounding: Q1 FY27 added the most >$100K ACV customers in company history, cRPO +21% and RPO +27% YoY, with AI-feature use in that cohort up to 37% from 21%
moat_justification: A real platform with developer mindshare, one-stack breadth across search/observability/security and genuine migration friction, plus ~75% gross margins — but no cycle of positive ROIC to show for it: the ROIC proxy is still negative in FY26, GAAP operating income is negative, hyperscalers fork and bundle against it, and SBC eats most of the cash the platform generates. That is a weak-to-narrow moat, not a durable wide one.
name: ELASTIC N.V.
one_liner: Real Search AI platform, moat 4/10, but owner's earnings are a rounding error after SBC — weighted IRR 3.3% and IV@15% $5.42 vs $95.25 price; it would need to fall to about $5.42 to clear a 15% hurdle on the current TTM base.
